fatal_errors: The proposed carbon-alloying intervention does not reconstruct the crystallographic loading-direction intervention examined in the target study.
No carbon concentration, processing route, temperature range, or strain-rate range is specified.

The suggested grain-refinement and precipitation-hardening mechanisms are unsupported and are not connected to the target mechanism of vacancy-assisted Shockley-partial nucleation and stacking-fault formation.
The predicted improvement is qualitative and does not define measurable strength and ductility criteria.
The falsification experiment lacks specified conditions, controls, microstructural diagnostics, and a quantitative rejection threshold.
explanation: The hypothesis addresses the same alloy family and broadly seeks improved dynamic strength–ductility performance relative to an unmodified baseline, but it otherwise has little agreement with the hidden target. The target concerns single-crystal anisotropy under <110>, <1-12>, and <-111> tensile loading at 10–600 K and 10^8–10^10 s^-1, with deformation mediated by Shockley partials and stacking faults. The generated proposal instead introduces unspecified carbon and conjectures grain refinement or precipitation hardening without evidence. It provides neither bounded conditions nor directional, temperature-dependent, or strain-rate-dependent predictions. Its generic comparative test could screen the idea, but it cannot sharply distinguish the proposed mechanisms or reproduce the target findings.
